questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: A sequence of rigid motions maps triangle ABC onto triangle DEF, taking A to D, B to E, and C to F. AB = 5 and angle B = 40°. Which side and which angle of DEF must equal these? Explain using rigid motions.
questions.prompt_markup:
A sequence of rigid motions maps triangle ABC onto triangle DEF, taking A to D, B to E, and C to F. AB = 5 and angle B = 40°.
Which side and which angle of DEF must equal these? Explain using rigid motions.
questions.correct_answer: DE = 5 and angle E = 40°: the rigid motions map segment AB onto DE and angle B onto angle E, and rigid motions keep lengths and angle measures.

sections.skill: Explain the SAS, ASA, and SSS criteria with rigid motions

questions.skill: Explain the SAS, ASA, and SSS criteria with rigid motions
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 10 as a second forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: Triangles ABC and DEF have AB = DE, angle A = angle D, and AC = DF (SAS). Explain the rigid motions that map triangle ABC onto triangle DEF, and why C must land on F.
questions.prompt_markup:
Triangles ABC and DEF have AB = DE, angle A = angle D, and AC = DF (SAS).
Explain the rigid motions that map triangle ABC onto triangle DEF, and why C must land on F.
questions.correct_answer: A rigid motion maps A to D, B to E, and C to F, so the triangles are congruent.
questions.required_method: A complete argument: translate A to D; rotate so ray AB lies along ray DE, and B lands on E because AB = DE; if C is on the other side of DE from F, reflect across DE. Since angle A = angle D, ray AC lies along ray DF, and since AC = DF, C lands on F. Any equivalent order is accepted.

questions.skill: Explain the SAS, ASA, and SSS criteria with rigid motions
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 10 as a second forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: Triangles ABC and DEF have angle A = angle D, AB = DE, and angle B = angle E (ASA). After rigid motions map segment AB onto segment DE (with C and F on the same side), explain why C must land on F.
questions.prompt_markup:
Triangles ABC and DEF have angle A = angle D, AB = DE, and angle B = angle E (ASA).
After rigid motions map segment AB onto segment DE (with C and F on the same side), explain why C must land on F.
questions.correct_answer: C lands on F, so the triangles are congruent.
questions.required_method: Because angle A = angle D, the image of ray AC lies along ray DF; because angle B = angle E, the image of ray BC lies along ray EF. C is on both rays, and the two rays meet at only one point, F.

questions.skill: Explain the SAS, ASA, and SSS criteria with rigid motions
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 10 as a second forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: Triangles ABC and DEF have AB = DE, BC = EF, and AC = DF (SSS). Rigid motions map AB onto DE, with C and F on the same side of DE. Explain why C must land on F.
questions.prompt_markup:
Triangles ABC and DEF have AB = DE, BC = EF, and AC = DF (SSS). Rigid motions map AB onto DE, with C and F on the same side of DE.
Explain why C must land on F.
questions.correct_answer: C is at distance AC from D and BC from E. On that side of DE, only one point (F) is at those two distances (the two circles meet there once), so C lands on F.
